items.title: A middle fact
items.prose: One of the facts people mix up most.
items.question: What is 6 × 8?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Step from a fact you trust, such as 5 × 8 = 40.

byKey.six-sevens: That is 6 × 7, one six short. 6 × 8 is 42 + 6.
byKey.six-nines: That is 6 × 9, one six too many. 6 × 8 is 54 − 6.
byKey.seven-eights: That is 7 × 8, one eight too many. 6 × 8 is 56 − 8.

explain.text: $5 \times 8 = 40$, and one more 8 makes 48. Its neighbours 42, 54 and 56 are the usual mix-ups.

items.title: The 12s by parts
items.prose: Twelve lots is ten lots plus two lots.
items.question: What is 12 × 9?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add ten nines and two nines.

byKey.eleven-nines: That is 11 × 9. Twelve lots is two lots more than ten, so add 18 to 90.
byKey.minus-two: You took 2 off 120. Nine twelves is 120 − 12 = 108.
byKey.side-by-side: You wrote 9 tens and 18 side by side. Add 90 and 18 instead.

explain.text: $10 \times 9 = 90$ and $2 \times 9 = 18$, so $12 \times 9 = 108$. The nines pattern agrees: $120 - 12 = 108$.

items.title: Split and carry
items.prose: Split the two-digit number into tens and units.
items.question: What is 8 × 67?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out 60 × 8 and 7 × 8, then add them.

byKey.side-by-side: You wrote 48 and 56 side by side. Add 480 and 56 instead.
byKey.dropped-carry: The tens make 8 + 5 = 13, which carries a hundred. 480 + 56 = 536.

explain.text: $60 \times 8 = 480$ and $7 \times 8 = 56$. Adding, the tens make $8 + 5 = 13$, which carries a hundred. So $8 \times 67 = 536$.

items.title: Eleven with a carry
items.prose: Use the 11 shortcut, or split 11 into 10 and 1.
items.question: What is 11 × 57?

options.why: You put 12 between 5 and 7. Carry its 1 into the hundreds: 627.
You kept the 2 of the 12 and dropped its 1. It makes 5 + 1 = 6 hundreds.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out 10 × 57, then add one more 57.

explain.text: $570 + 57 = 627$. In the shortcut, $5 + 7 = 12$, so the 1 carries and 5 becomes 6. The answer reads 6, 2, 7.

items.title: Four pieces
items.prose: Four people work out $12 \times 63$ with the grid method.
items.question: Whose working is complete and right?

options.why: This person multiplied tens by tens and units by units. Two pieces are missing: $10 \times 3$ and $2 \times 60$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check that each working has all four pieces.

explain.text: The pieces are $10 \times 60$, $10 \times 3$, $2 \times 60$ and $2 \times 3$. They add to $600 + 30 + 120 + 6 = 756$. Row by row it is $630 + 126$, the same total.

items.title: Just under 100
items.prose: Round 98 up to 100, then pay back the gap.
items.question: What is 4 × 98?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The gap is 2, and each unit of it is a lot of 4.

byKey.gap-only: You took off the gap, 2. Each unit of the gap is a lot of 4, so take off 8.
byKey.one-lot: You took off one lot of 4. 98 is two short of 100, so two lots come off.
byKey.added: You added the payback. 98 is below 100, so it comes off.

explain.text: $4 \times 100 = 400$. 98 is 2 short, so two lots of 4 come off. $400 - 8 = 392$.

items.title: A broker fee
items.prose: A broker charges a 3% fee on a £1,200 trade. 3% means 3 for every 100.
items.question: What is the fee, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the hundreds in £1,200, then charge £3 for each.

byKey.point-three: That is 0.3%. Each 100 costs a whole 3 pounds.
byKey.thirds: You divided by 3. A 3% fee is 3 for every 100.
byKey.gross: That is the trade plus the fee. The question asks for the fee alone.

explain.text: £1,200 is 12 hundreds. Each hundred costs £3 in fees, so the fee is $12 \times 3 = 36$ pounds. Count the hundreds first, then it is a table fact.

items.title: A return on a notional
items.prose: A £400,000 position returns 2.5% in a month. As a decimal that is 0.025, and $0.025 = \tfrac{25}{1000}$.
items.question: What is the profit, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. 0.025 is 25 thousandths. Divide by 1,000, then multiply by 25.

byKey.twenty-five: That is 0.25 of the book. 0.025 is ten times smaller.
byKey.point-25: That is 0.0025 of the book. 0.025 is ten times bigger.
byKey.halved-once: That is 50 lots of £400. Halve again for 25 lots.

explain.text: £400,000 ÷ 1,000 = £400. 25 lots of £400 is a quarter of 100 lots, £40,000, so £10,000. It is the ×25 move: a quarter of a round number.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add 100, two strips of 80, and 64.

byKey.each-part: You squared 10 and 8 and added. The two strips, 80 each, are missing.
byKey.one-strip: You counted one strip of 80. There are two.
byKey.doubled: You doubled 18. Squaring means 18 lots of 18.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The gap from 20 is 3, so take off $3^2$.

byKey.one: You took off 1, as for $19 \times 21$. Here the gap is 3, so take off $3^2 = 9$.
byKey.gap-not-squared: You took off the gap, 3. The corner is 3 by 3, so take off 9.
byKey.added: You added the corner. In $(20 - 3)(20 + 3)$ the corner is $-9$.
